clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Anons on /biz/ are debating which one survives the next decade, and both sides think the other side is a boomer.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ debate on whether to hold BTC or gold for the long term

signal.rationale: OP framing favors BTC as the long-term store of value over gold, implicit long bias

clips.text_en_b2: The age-old question keeps resurfacing across /biz/: if you had to hold a single asset for the next ten years, would you go with Bitcoin or gold? What makes your pick superior to the alternative? Anons are going head to head, and although both camps claim the other side is stuck in the past, nobody is budging an inch.
clips.text_en_c1: The eternal question keeps resurfacing on /biz/: if you were forced to hold a single asset for the coming decade, would your money be on Bitcoin or gold? Gold advocates cite its track record as the ultimate store of value, whereas Bitcoin maximalists argue that digital scarcity, network effects, and programmability render gold obsolete for younger generations. Each camp dismisses the other as hopelessly out of touch, convinced that the opposing side simply cannot grasp what monetary sovereignty will look like in 2035. The thread has become a microcosm of generational divides.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial question resurfaces yet again: if one were compelled to hold a single asset through the coming decade, would Bitcoin or gold merit the allocation? Predictably, the risk-averse contingent champions bullion on the grounds of its historical resilience, whereas the conviction holders contend that such prudence is, in essence, an abdication of ambition. Anons on /biz/ have once more devolved into mutual recrimination, each faction dismissing the other as relics of a bygone financial era, incapable of grasping the asymmetric upside that a digitally native, deflationary instrument purportedly affords. The thread, as ever, is less an exercise in analysis than a referendum on temperament.

clips.text_en_c1: A thread circulating on /biz/ floats an audacious proposition: acquire a fleet of Tesla Cybercabs and deploy them onto the Robotaxi network as a hands-free revenue stream. The pitch is deceptively elegant, since no chauffeur, no managerial overhead, and minimal maintenance would translate into what enthusiasts describe as a money printer operating quietly in the background. Sceptics, however, contend that the entire thesis rests on vapourware, regulatory wishful thinking, and the delusions of bagholders desperate to rationalise sunken costs. Whether it constitutes genuine financial liberation or merely elaborate cope remains firmly contested.
clips.text_en_c2: The proposition under discussion on /biz/ is as seductive as it is fantastical: one purchases a fleet of Tesla Cybercabs, enrols them on the proprietary Robotaxi network, and thereafter reaps a passive income stream while remaining entirely insulated from the operational exigencies of driving, staffing, or maintenance. In essence, capital is converted into a self-executing revenue-generating instrument, untethered from human intervention. Whether this constitutes a credible financial egress or merely the elaborate cope of bagholders desperate to rationalise their positions remains, predictably, a matter of fervent contention, with sceptics invoking the usual litany of regulatory uncertainty.

clips.text_zh: OK 真係頂唔順💀 本地LLM 真係廢 問啲basic嘢都答錯曬 燒錢燒時間仲要比人笑 同我考HKIE一樣辛苦lol
clips.text_en_b1: Local AI is a complete joke. I asked my local LLM how far the earth is from the sun and it told me the sun is the 3rd largest planet and earth is 4 miles away. Total scam. Why does anyone waste time and money on this garbage?
clips.source_hint: /g/ rant about local LLMs failing basic questions
clips.text_en_b2: Local AI is honestly a complete joke at this point. I threw a basic question at my local LLM, asking how far the earth sits from the sun, and it confidently claimed the sun is the third largest planet while earth is a mere four miles away. Total scam. Why on earth would anyone keep burning time and money on this garbage?
clips.text_en_c1: Local large language models are, frankly, an embarrassment to anyone who values their time and electricity bill. When prompted with something as elementary as the distance between Earth and the sun, a certain model confidently declared that the sun ranks as the third-largest planet and that our planet sits a meagre four miles away. Beyond the absurdity of the response lies a more troubling pattern: hallucinated facts dressed up in authoritative prose, hours of computation evaporating into confidently incorrect nonsense. Until these systems demonstrate elementary competence, enthusiasm for running them locally remains entirely unjustifiable.
clips.text_en_c2: The premise of running large language models locally, once heralded as a sovereign alternative to corporate APIs, has revealed itself, in practice, to be a thoroughly disillusioning endeavour. Even the most rudimentary factual inquiries elicit responses so catastrophically erroneous that one is compelled to question the very utility of the exercise; my own local model, when queried about the earth-sun distance, confidently asserted that the sun constitutes the third-largest planet, with our planet a mere four miles distant. The cumulative expenditure of compute and electricity, set against such abject failure, renders the entire proposition little more than an elaborate exercise in self-flagellation.

clips.text_en_b2: A bizarre new trend has just dropped in China, and it is spreading like wildfire. Chinese netizens are calling it the "bubble chin," and it is rapidly catching on among mainland female influencers. Photos are circulating across /pol/ tonight, with anons divided on whether the look is actually cute or genuinely cursed.
clips.text_en_c1: An emerging aesthetic trend on the Chinese internet, colloquially dubbed the bubble chin, is rapidly gaining traction among female influencers across major platforms. The procedure, which produces an unusually pronounced and rounded chin contour, has divided opinion sharply, with admirers praising its youthful, almost doll-like charm while detractors dismiss it as visually grotesque. Screenshots have proliferated across /pol/ tonight, where anons are split between those who find it endearing and those who consider it cursed. Hong Kong audiences, predictably, seem entirely uninterested in importing the look.
clips.text_en_c2: A new aesthetic aberration has begun proliferating amongst Chinese female influencers, colloquially termed the 'bubble chin,' whose proponents evidently regard it as the apogee of contemporary beauty, whilst sceptics discern something altogether more unsettling in the distended submandibular contours on display. Photographs have circulated with alacrity across /pol/ this evening, occasioning a schism within the community that mirrors broader anxieties about the trajectory of Chinese cultural exports. Whether the trend portends genuine adoption or merely constitutes a transient curiosity, derided and swiftly discarded, remains to be seen.

clips.text_zh: OK 唔做嘢嘅夜晚就係打機 /v/有人問Fallout 4係咪真係好似大家講咁好 有人話rushed 有人話神作 我就覺得OK打發時間ok
clips.text_en_b1: Is Fallout 4 really as good as people say it is? When I first played it, it felt like a game that was developed too quickly and rushed to release. Other anons say it is still one of the best open world RPGs of the last decade.
clips.text_en_b2: Is Fallout 4 genuinely worth the hype people keep giving it? When I first fired it up, it struck me as a title that had clearly been rushed out the door to meet a deadline. Other anons insist it still stands among the finest open-world RPGs of the past decade, while skeptics argue it was cooked far too quickly.
clips.text_en_c1: On a slow evening thread over at /v/, the perennial debate resurfaces: does Fallout 4 genuinely deserve the acclaim it accumulated at launch, or is the praise largely retrospective nostalgia? Certain anons argue that the title bears all the hallmarks of a project rushed to meet commercial deadlines, with diluted writing and underdeveloped factions betraying production pressures. Defenders counter that, despite its imperfections, the game remains among the most engaging open-world RPGs of its generation, offering dozens of hours of compelling exploration. Personally, I find it perfectly serviceable as a time-killer between more demanding releases.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial debate over Fallout 4's legacy has resurfaced on /v/, occasioned no doubt by another idle evening of disinclination towards productivity. One faction contends that the title bears all the hallmarks of a project expedited to meet commercial imperatives, its seams plainly visible beneath a veneer of post-apocalyptic polish; the opposing camp maintains that, notwithstanding any developmental compromises, the game remains amongst the most accomplished open-world role-playing experiences of the past decade. The thread, predictably, has devolved into a proxy conflict over nostalgia and taste, with neither side likely to relinquish their entrenched position.

clips.text_en_b2: Solid bench press, anon, 315 lbs is genuinely impressive. Now picture yourself getting folded in half on the mat by someone who actually trains grappling. You have absolutely no excuse to skip it unless you want a guy fifty pounds lighter to make you his personal chew toy. clips.text_en_c1: Congratulations on your bench press, anonymous; three hundred and fifteen pounds is undeniably impressive within the confines of a commercial gym. However, raw strength becomes almost irrelevant the moment a competent grappler closes the distance and initiates a takedown. Any practitioner with a rudimentary grasp of Brazilian jiu-jitsu could dismantle a pure powerlifter half their size within seconds, leaving them contorted into positions they never knew their bodies could achieve. If you genuinely value functional capability over mirror aesthetics, supplementing your barbell work with mat time is non-negotiable, no matter how taxing it proves.
clips.text_en_c2: The bench press enthusiast, having dutifully conveyed three hundred and fifteen pounds from floor to chest, is nonetheless gently reminded that such linear-progression achievements in the iron game pale into insignificance the moment a grappling exchange is initiated; any competent practitioner, irrespective of a substantial weight disadvantage, possesses the requisite toolkit to contort the hapless deadlifter into positions of exquisite submission. The gym's resident strongmen, it must be conceded, remain conspicuously reticent when confronted with the proposition that their hypertrophied musculature confers no particular immunity on the mat, a fact that the initiated find deliciously irrefutable.
